Determine simulation window from weather data

Source: R/epicrop_sim.R
dot-determine_run_window.Rd

Extracts the subset of weather data needed for the simulation based on the emergence date and simulation duration. Validates that sufficient weather data is available for the requested time window.

Usage

.determine_run_window(wth, emergence, duration)

Arguments

wth

A data.table containing weather data with daily time-step. Must have a column YYYYMMDD of class Date containing the date for each observation. This is typically an object of class epicrop.wth created by get_wth() or format_wth().

emergence

Character string or Date object specifying the crop emergence date in YYYY-MM-DD format. If a vector is provided, only the first element is used (with a warning).

duration

Integer specifying the number of days to simulate from the emergence date. Must be a positive integer, typically >= 50 days for meaningful disease progression.

Value

A list with two elements:

wth_subset

A data.table subset of the input weather data containing exactly duration rows, starting from the emergence date. This is the weather data that will be used for the simulation.

run_dates

A Date vector of length duration containing the sequence of dates for the simulation window, starting from the emergence date.

Details

This function performs several operations:

  1. Converts the emergence date to Date class using .check_date()

  2. Generates a sequence of dates from emergence to emergence + duration - 1

  3. Ensures the weather data's YYYYMMDD column is Date class for matching

  4. Extracts rows from the weather data that match the simulation dates

  5. Validates that the extracted data has exactly duration rows

If multiple emergence dates are provided, only the first is used and a warning is issued.

If insufficient weather data is available (the extracted subset has fewer than duration rows), an informative error is thrown showing:

  • The requested number of days

  • The actual number of days available

  • The requested date window

  • The available date range in the weather data

Side Effects

  • Prints an informative message showing the emergence date

  • May modify the input wth data.table in place to convert YYYYMMDD to Date class if it isn't already

See also

  • .check_date() for date parsing and validation

  • get_wth() for fetching weather data from NASA POWER

  • format_wth() for formatting user-supplied weather data

  • epicrop_sim() which calls this function internally

Author

Adam H. Sparks, adamhsparks@gmail.com

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# This is an internal function not meant to be called directly
wth <- get_wth(
  lonlat = c(121.25562, 14.6774),
  dates = c("2000-06-30", "2000-12-31")
)

# Extract 120-day window starting July 1
run_info <- epicrop:::.determine_run_window(
  wth = wth,
  emergence = "2000-07-01",
  duration = 120
)

# Check the results
nrow(run_info$wth_subset)  # 120
length(run_info$run_dates)  # 120
range(run_info$run_dates)  # 2000-07-01 to 2000-10-28
} # }
